t: You're standing by Euston House, on Eversholt Street, which was called Seymour Street when the building went up in 1934. It was built as the headquarters of the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, one of the great railway companies of its day. Later it served as the headquarters of the British Railways Board. It was designed by Albert Victor Heal, an architect and designer based in England who held the Military Cross and was a Fellow of the Royal Institute of British Architects.
